To generate DNS records for each autonomous system on the Internet
To encrypt routing updates exchanged between peer routers
explain: A flapping or failed BGP peer can change or break Internet reachability and often signals a provider fault or a configuration error. Alerting on session state lets engineers react before users report widespread connectivity loss.

q: What is the purpose of sending maintenance notifications before a scheduled change window?
options: To inform only the technical staff who will perform the change
To keep the details of the maintenance hidden from affected users
To warn affected users in advance of possible service disruption
To obtain vendor approval after the change has been completed
explain: Advance notice tells users when a disruption may occur, which reduces surprise and helpdesk calls during the window. Notifications go to the affected users, not just the staff performing the work.

q: A site-to-site VPN tunnel fails and the logs show certificate validation errors; the peer certificate expired the previous day. What is the best action?
options: Renew the certificate and implement monitoring for certificate expiry
Disable certificate validation on both VPN peer devices
Reboot both VPN gateways and clear the error logs
Change the tunnel to use a weaker encryption algorithm
explain: An expired certificate fails validation, so the tunnel cannot be established until a valid certificate is installed. Monitoring expiry dates prevents the same silent failure from recurring on other tunnels.

q: What does a campus area network (CAN) typically connect?
options: Multiple buildings within a nearby campus or corporate park
Wireless devices located within one person's immediate area
Branch offices located in different countries around the world
Two devices paired directly over a short-range Bluetooth link
explain: A CAN interconnects the LANs of nearby buildings, such as those on a university or corporate campus. It is larger than a single-building LAN but smaller than a metropolitan or wide area network.

q: How should decommissioned network equipment that stored sensitive configuration data be disposed of?
options: Through the general office trash collection service
By donating it immediately without wiping the stored data
By storing it indefinitely in an unlocked equipment closet
Through certified recyclers that provide sanitization documentation
explain: Certified recyclers sanitize or destroy storage and media and provide certificates of destruction for audit purposes. Discarding or donating equipment without sanitization risks exposing credentials and network details.

q: A primary WAN link fails, but traffic does not move to the backup link. What should be checked first?
options: The speed and duplex settings configured on user workstations
The DNS records published by the backup service provider
The labeling applied to cables in the distribution frame
The tracking objects and failure thresholds that trigger failover
explain: Failover depends on tracking, such as IP SLA probes, detecting the failure and crossing a configured threshold before the backup route is installed. If the probe still reports the dead link as healthy, or thresholds are misconfigured, failover never triggers.

q: What do link-state routing protocols such as OSPF build in order to calculate routes?
options: Only the address of the next-hop router for each destination
A list of routes learned only from directly connected neighbors
A complete topology map of the entire routing area
A static route table that is never updated after startup
explain: Link-state protocols flood link-state advertisements so every router holds the same complete topology map, then run Dijkstra's algorithm to compute the shortest path. Distance-vector protocols, by contrast, know only next-hop information from neighbors.

q: What does service-level agreement (SLA) monitoring measure?
options: Internal switch port speed and duplex settings on the LAN
User satisfaction scores collected by the helpdesk team
Provider performance compared with the contracted service levels
The quality of application source code used by network tools
explain: SLA monitoring tracks provider latency, packet loss, and uptime against the levels promised in the contract. Those measurements are the evidence used to hold the carrier accountable and claim service credits for misses.

q: What should troubleshooting documentation include to be most useful for the next incident?
options: Only the name of the person judged responsible for the fault
Only a brief statement confirming that the issue was fixed
The findings, the actions taken, and the final outcomes
Only the configuration of devices that were not changed
explain: Documenting what was found, what was done, and what resulted builds a knowledge base the next engineer can search. Records that contain only the final fix, or blame, leave out the reasoning that makes the entry reusable.

q: What advantage does Variable Length Subnet Masking (VLSM) provide?
options: It allows subnets of different sizes within a single network
It summarizes multiple networks into one route advertisement
It translates private addresses to a public address for Internet access
It assigns IP addresses automatically to hosts on each subnet
explain: VLSM lets each subnet use the mask that fits its host count, so a point-to-point link can take a /30 while a user segment takes a /24, wasting far fewer addresses. Route summarization, NAT, and DHCP are separate techniques with different purposes.

q: A switch port uses port security with the violation mode set to shutdown. What happens when an unauthorized frame arrives on that port?
options: The port logs a warning but continues forwarding the traffic
The port is placed into the err-disabled state
The port dynamically moves itself into a different VLAN
The switch reboots itself to clear the security violation
explain: In shutdown mode a violation err-disables the port, and an administrator or a recovery timer must restore it. The restrict mode is the less disruptive alternative: it drops the offending traffic and logs the violation while the port stays up.

q: What is attenuation in network cabling?
options: Interference induced by an external electromagnetic source
The encryption applied to a signal before it is transmitted
The loss of signal strength as the signal travels over distance
The increase in signal strength provided by an amplifier
explain: Attenuation is the gradual weakening of a signal over the length of a cable, which is why media have maximum distance limits. It is different from interference, which adds unwanted noise to the signal from outside sources.

q: Users report that the network becomes slow at the same time every day but performs well at other times. What should the administrator investigate first?
options: Whether a single workstation has developed a faulty network adapter
Whether every switch port has been assigned to the correct VLAN
Whether scheduled backups or jobs are saturating links, and how QoS is applied
Whether the horizontal cabling in the building exceeds its maximum length
explain: A problem that follows the clock usually follows a schedule, and backups, replication, and update jobs can saturate links at set times. Reviewing those schedules and shaping the traffic with QoS addresses the congestion without changing cabling that works the rest of the day.

q: What is the purpose of Quality of Service (QoS) on a congested network?
options: To prioritize critical traffic when bandwidth is limited
To increase the physical bandwidth available on every link
To encrypt voice traffic before it leaves the local network
To assign IP addresses to devices based on traffic priority
explain: QoS classifies and queues traffic so latency-sensitive applications such as voice keep working when a link is congested. It does not create additional bandwidth; it decides which traffic is served first when there is not enough for everything.

q: A workstation is connected to a switch port, but the port's link light is off. What does this most likely indicate?
options: The workstation has been assigned to the wrong VLAN
The workstation is configured with an incorrect DNS server
The application on the workstation is using the wrong port number
There is no physical connectivity on that link
explain: The link light reflects Layer 1 connectivity, so a dark light points to the cable, the port, the far-end device, or speed negotiation. VLAN, DNS, and application settings are higher-layer issues that would not extinguish the link light.

q: Which mnemonic lists the OSI model layers in order from Layer 1 (bottom) to Layer 7 (top)?
options: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away
All People Seem To Need Data Processing
Please Do Not Throw Pizza Sausage Away
All Professionals Should Try New Deserts
explain: 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away' maps to Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application, from the bottom up. 'All People Seem To Need Data Processing' lists the same layers in the opposite, top-down direction.

q: Which description best fits a standard change in change management?
options: An unplanned change made in reaction to a major incident
A pre-approved, low-risk, routine change
An emergency change that bypasses the approval process
A major change requiring full advisory board review every time
explain: Standard changes are routine, low-risk, and follow a procedure that has already been approved, such as a recurring patch or password reset, so they do not need full board approval each time. Emergency and major changes follow stricter paths.

q: How does TCP establish a connection before data is sent?
options: With a four-way handshake that uses FIN and ACK flags
With a three-way handshake using SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK
Without any handshake, by sending data immediately
With a two-way handshake that uses only SYN and ACK
explain: TCP opens a connection with SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK, which synchronizes sequence numbers in both directions before data flows. The four-way FIN exchange is how a TCP connection is closed, and sending data with no handshake describes UDP.

q: How many bits are contained in one nibble?
options: 2 bits
4 bits
8 bits
16 bits
explain: A nibble is 4 bits, so two nibbles make up one 8-bit byte. Because 4 bits express exactly one hexadecimal digit, nibbles are a convenient way to read binary and IPv6 addresses.

q: What is the purpose of the Frame Check Sequence (FCS) field in an Ethernet frame?
options: To encrypt the frame payload to keep its contents confidential
To detect transmission errors by using a cyclic redundancy check value
To carry the destination MAC address used for local delivery
To identify the upper-layer protocol that the frame is carrying
explain: The sender computes a CRC and stores it in the FCS field, and the receiver recomputes it to check for corruption. A frame whose check fails is discarded rather than delivered with damaged data.

q: How does an application-layer (Layer 7) denial-of-service attack differ from a volumetric attack?
options: It floods network bandwidth with a large volume of junk traffic
It corrupts DNS records so users are redirected to false servers
It exploits faults in physical cabling to interrupt the service
It targets Layer 7 using requests that appear to be valid
explain: Layer 7 attacks such as HTTP floods and Slowloris use small numbers of seemingly legitimate requests to exhaust application resources, so simple bandwidth filtering does not stop them. Defending against them requires behavioral analysis and web application firewall controls.

q: A cable tester shows that the transmit and receive pairs are reversed on a run. How should this fault be corrected?
options: Correct the cable termination, or use a crossover cable or Auto-MDIX where appropriate
Move the cable away from sources of electromagnetic interference
Shorten the cable run so it falls within the maximum length
Configure the switch port to operate at a lower negotiated speed
explain: Reversed pairs are a termination error, so the run should be re-terminated to the correct pinout; Auto-MDIX or a crossover cable can compensate in the meantime. Interference, excess length, and speed settings are different faults with different symptoms.

q: What do NetFlow, sFlow, and IPFIX provide to network administrators?
options: Complete packet payloads captured from every conversation
Encryption for traffic flowing between network devices
Traffic flow metadata exported for analysis and monitoring
Routing updates exchanged between different autonomous systems
explain: Flow technologies export metadata about conversations, including source and destination, ports, protocol, and byte counts, without storing full payloads. That record is ideal for capacity planning, anomaly detection, and investigating who communicated with whom.

q: How do devices share the medium in a token ring topology?
options: Each device passes a token in order around a circular ring
Each device connects to a central switch in a star pattern
Devices transmit whenever the medium is idle, using CSMA/CD
Devices are attached along a line terminated at both ends
explain: In a ring, a token circulates from device to device and only the token holder may transmit, which gives orderly access. A single break can disrupt a simple ring, which is why dual-ring designs such as FDDI were used for resilience.

q: Testing confirms that a keystone jack is faulty and causing intermittent connectivity. What is the best course of action?
options: Repair the internal contacts of the jack and return it to service
Bypass the jack and plug the horizontal cable directly into the switch
Reserve the jack for voice traffic instead of data traffic
Replace the jack with a new keystone jack and retest the run
explain: Keystone jacks are inexpensive, consumable components and are not designed to be repaired once their contacts fail. Replacing the jack and retesting the run restores the link to a known-good standard.

q: Why should a technician try to reproduce a network problem in a lab environment?
options: To validate a theory safely without risking the production network
To postpone resolution until the vendor can join the investigation
To generate extra test traffic on the live production network
To remove the need to document findings from the production incident
explain: Reproducing a fault in the lab lets the technician test theories and candidate fixes where a mistake cannot extend an outage. Changes proven in the lab can then be applied to production with much lower risk.

q: What does the VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP) do on Cisco switches?
options: It routes traffic between VLANs that use different subnets
It assigns switch ports to VLANs based on device MAC addresses
It synchronizes the VLAN database across multiple switches
It encrypts trunk traffic passing between connected switches
explain: VTP advertises VLAN configuration from a server switch so client switches share the same VLAN database, which reduces manual configuration. It must be used carefully, because a switch with a higher revision number can overwrite the VLAN database of the whole domain.

q: Interface counters show steadily increasing CRC and input errors on a switch port. What do these counters most likely reveal?
options: That the DHCP address pool for the VLAN is nearly exhausted
That DNS records for the connected hosts are about to expire
That there are physical-layer problems such as faulty cabling or a duplex mismatch
That the routing protocol has finished converging on all routers
explain: CRC and input errors accumulate when frames arrive damaged, which points to Layer 1 causes such as bad cabling, faulty connectors, or a duplex mismatch. Output drops, by contrast, usually indicate congestion rather than corruption.

q: In wireless networking, what is an Independent Basic Service Set (IBSS)?
options: A network where clients connect directly to each other without an access point
A network where clients connect through a controller managing many access points
A network in which a single access point provides infrastructure service
A network that extends coverage by coordinating several access points
explain: An IBSS is the ad-hoc mode of 802.11, in which stations communicate peer-to-peer with no access point coordinating them. Infrastructure networks, in both standalone and controller-based forms, are built around access points instead.

q: What is multiplexing in data communications?
options: Converting an analog signal into a digital signal for transmission
Directing packets toward the correct destination network
Combining multiple signals so they can share a single medium
Encrypting several data streams with one shared secret key
explain: Multiplexing lets many conversations share one expensive link, using techniques such as time-division, frequency-division, and wavelength-division multiplexing. Each channel is separated again at the far end by demultiplexing.

q: What is the purpose of rogue access point detection on an enterprise wireless network?
options: To locate unauthorized access points connected to the network
To improve the signal strength of authorized access points
To assign radio channels automatically to all access points
To authenticate users before they join the wireless network
explain: A rogue access point, whether installed by an employee or an attacker as an evil twin, creates an uncontrolled entry point into the wired network. Wireless intrusion prevention systems detect such devices so they can be located, contained, and removed.

q: Which data rates are QSFP transceiver modules commonly used to provide?
options: Ethernet connections running at 10 Mbps and 100 Mbps
Ethernet connections running at 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps
Ethernet connections running at 40 Gbps and 100 Gbps
SONET connections running at 155 Mbps and 622 Mbps
explain: QSFP modules combine four lanes in one transceiver, which is how they deliver aggregate rates such as 40 Gbps and 100 Gbps for switch uplinks and data center links. The smaller SFP and SFP+ modules serve the 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps tiers.

q: What are the primary design goals of the core layer in a hierarchical network design?
options: High speed, redundancy, and low-latency forwarding
Applying detailed access policies to individual user traffic
Providing direct access connections for end-user PCs
Performing user authentication and port security checks
explain: The core is kept simple and fast, with redundant paths, so traffic crosses the backbone with minimal delay and no policy processing to slow it down. Policy enforcement belongs to the distribution layer and end-device connectivity to the access layer.

q: In load balancing, what does gracefully draining a server accomplish?
options: It immediately terminates every client connection to that server
It removes the server's DNS records without notifying any clients
It redirects all traffic instantly onto a single backup server
It stops new connections while allowing existing sessions to finish
explain: Draining prevents the load balancer from sending new sessions to a server while letting current sessions complete normally. That makes it possible to patch or retire the server with no visible interruption to users.

q: When planning Power over Ethernet (PoE) for a switch, what must the administrator ensure?
options: That every switch port is configured to deliver its maximum wattage
That the total power drawn by powered devices stays within the switch's PoE budget
That powered devices receive power only through standalone injectors
That the wattage calculation is based only on the length of each cable
explain: Each switch has a finite PoE power budget shared across its ports, so the administrator must total the draw of all cameras, phones, and access points. Exceeding the budget can cause devices to fail to power up or to drop when additional load is added.

q: How many usable host addresses does an IPv4 /26 subnet provide?
options: 62 usable host addresses
64 usable host addresses
126 usable host addresses
30 usable host addresses
explain: A /26 leaves 6 host bits, giving 2^6 = 64 total addresses, minus the network and broadcast addresses, which leaves 62 usable hosts. The 126-address figure belongs to a /25, and 30 addresses to a /27.

q: What is the purpose of a hardware security module (HSM)?
options: To speed up user authentication by caching account passwords
To store backup copies of device configuration files offline
To protect cryptographic keys inside dedicated tamper-resistant hardware
To provide software-based encryption services for virtual machines
explain: An HSM generates, stores, and uses private keys inside hardened hardware so the keys never have to be exposed in general-purpose software. HSMs commonly anchor certificate authority roots and other high-value PKI operations.

q: Which packet capture approach best helps an engineer find where packets are being lost on a path?
options: Capturing traffic at multiple points along the path at the same time
Capturing traffic only at the destination, after the problem has cleared
Capturing traffic on a single network segment unrelated to the problem
Capturing only packet headers, without recording any timing information
explain: Simultaneous captures at several points can be compared to see exactly on which segment packets disappear. A single capture shows only what arrived at that one location, which cannot isolate the loss point.

q: What does software-defined networking (SDN) separate?
options: Network users from administrators on the management network
Wired connections from wireless connections across the campus
The control plane from the data (forwarding) plane
Management traffic from production user traffic on the same links
explain: SDN moves decision-making into a centralized controller (the control plane) while switches and routers keep forwarding packets (the data plane). That separation is what makes the network programmable through the controller.

q: A core router reports sustained high memory utilization. What should the administrator investigate?
options: Whether the cable runs connected to the router exceed their rated length
Whether spanning tree has blocked too many redundant switch ports
Whether workstations on the LAN are using statically assigned addresses
Whether large routing tables, such as full BGP tables, or a memory leak are consuming memory
explain: High memory use risks instability and crashes, and on a router it is commonly driven by very large routing tables or a software memory leak. Checking table sizes and memory trends identifies whether capacity planning or a software upgrade is the right remedy.

q: In IPv6, how does the EUI-64 format generate an interface identifier?
options: By deriving the identifier from the device's configured hostname
By generating the identifier randomly in order to preserve privacy
By obtaining the identifier from a DHCPv6 server assignment
By deriving the identifier from the device's MAC address
explain: EUI-64 builds the 64-bit interface ID from the 48-bit MAC address by inserting FFFE in the middle and flipping the universal/local bit. Privacy extensions were introduced because this predictable, MAC-based address allows a host to be tracked.

q: What does alert correlation do in a network monitoring system?
options: It increases the number of individual alerts sent to on-call staff
It groups related alerts together into a single incident
It suppresses all alerts that occur during normal business hours
It forwards every generated alert directly to the service provider
explain: One root-cause failure can trigger dozens of device alerts, and correlation combines those related alerts into a single incident. Engineers then work one problem instead of chasing a flood of separate notifications.

q: Users report that file transfers across the WAN are unusually slow. Which set of factors should be checked?
options: Duplex mismatches, SMB signing overhead, and the effects of WAN latency
DNS zone transfer settings and the duration of DHCP address leases
Wireless channel selection and whether the SSID is being broadcast
Printer queue settings and the permissions on local file shares
explain: File protocols such as SMB are sensitive to latency, and signing overhead plus a duplex mismatch can cut throughput sharply on a WAN link. Checking those factors, and WAN optimization where appropriate, addresses the usual causes of slow transfers.

q: Why is out-of-band management important when making changes to network devices?
options: It carries the primary data path used by ordinary user traffic
It provides alternate management access if in-band access is lost
It allows administrative users to bypass authentication requirements
It encrypts all production traffic for the duration of the change
explain: Out-of-band access, such as a console server or a separate management network, gives an engineer a way back into a device if a change breaks normal SSH access. Without it, a single bad change can lock the team out of the device entirely.

q: How is the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) correctly classified?
options: As a path-vector exterior gateway protocol
As a hybrid interior gateway protocol
As a distance-vector interior gateway protocol
As a link-state interior gateway protocol
explain: BGP runs between autonomous systems, making it an exterior gateway protocol, and it selects routes using AS-path information, which makes it a path-vector protocol. It exchanges updates over TCP port 179.

q: How does IP Source Guard help prevent IP address spoofing on a switch access port?
options: By encrypting all traffic that enters the access port
By filtering traffic against the DHCP snooping binding table
By inspecting application payloads for malicious content
By blocking all traffic that originates outside the local VLAN
explain: IP Source Guard checks each packet's source IP and MAC against the bindings learned by DHCP snooping and drops packets that do not match. That stops a host on the port from impersonating another host's address.

q: A site-to-site VPN tunnel repeatedly goes down and comes back up. What should be checked to find the cause?
options: Whether users have been assigned to the correct security groups
Whether the DNS forwarders are pointing to the correct servers
Whether the cables at both sites have been labeled at each end
Whether Dead Peer Detection settings, security association lifetimes, and ISP link stability are healthy
explain: Tunnel flapping is commonly caused by mismatched phase lifetimes forcing constant renegotiation, Dead Peer Detection tearing the tunnel down, or an unstable underlying Internet link. Comparing the peer configurations and checking link stability addresses all three.

q: What is the purpose of TCP maximum segment size (MSS) clamping on a VPN interface?
options: To adjust the TCP segment size to account for tunnel overhead
To raise the interface MTU above the physical link limit
To apply TCP header compression to traffic carried over UDP
To force every TCP connection to use the same window size
explain: Tunnel encapsulation consumes bytes, so packets at the normal MTU would need fragmentation or be dropped. Clamping the MSS lowers the segment size hosts use, so the encapsulated packets still fit through the tunnel.

q: Which set of problems is commonly associated with double NAT, where traffic passes through two layers of address translation?
options: VoIP and gaming connectivity problems, and failures of UPnP port mapping
DNSSEC validation failures and expired website certificates
Wireless roaming failures and areas of weak signal coverage
Duplex mismatches and rising CRC error counts on switches
explain: Two NAT layers break inbound connections and peer-to-peer applications, and UPnP can open a port on only one of the two devices, so VoIP and online gaming commonly suffer. Bridging the ISP gateway or removing one NAT layer resolves the condition.

q: Which statement about using jumbo frames across a WAN or the Internet is correct?
options: Jumbo frames are supported end-to-end by all Internet providers
Jumbo frames are required for every WAN connection to function
Jumbo frames reduce the MTU of every link on the path to 1500 bytes
Jumbo frames are usually not supported end-to-end across a WAN
explain: Jumbo frames only work when every device on the path supports the same large MTU, which cannot be guaranteed across the Internet, where 1500 bytes is the standard. They are therefore normally confined to controlled environments such as data center storage networks.

q: What is a demonstrated benefit of an ongoing security awareness training program?
options: It removes the need for technical email filtering controls
It replaces the need for multifactor authentication on accounts
It reduces the rate at which employees click phishing links
It guarantees that employees will never fall for a phishing attempt
explain: Regular training combined with simulated phishing measurably lowers click rates and increases reporting of suspicious messages. It reduces human risk but does not eliminate it, so technical controls such as filtering and MFA are still required.

q: One peer of a site-to-site VPN is missing the route to the remote network. What is the most likely result?
options: Traffic will be NAT-translated and forwarded outside the tunnel
Traffic will flow in only one direction through the tunnel
The tunnel will create the missing route automatically on both peers
Traffic will be forwarded through a different tunnel by default
explain: If one side has no route back, packets can leave through the tunnel but replies have no path home, producing one-way traffic. Verifying that routes and the traffic selectors mirror each other on both peers is a standard VPN check.

q: Why does a public key infrastructure (PKI) use a hierarchy of root, intermediate, and issuing certificate authorities?
options: It limits exposure of the root CA, which stays offline while intermediates issue certificates
It removes the need to protect the root CA private key at all
It allows every workstation on the network to act as a certificate authority
It makes certificates trusted without any validation of the chain
explain: Keeping the root offline and using it only to sign intermediates protects the trust anchor of the whole PKI. If an intermediate is compromised it can be revoked and replaced without rebuilding trust in the root on every device.

q: What should monitoring of an SD-WAN deployment primarily track?
options: Only whether each device responds to simple SNMP polls
Only the physical link status of each WAN circuit
Only the number of users connected at each remote site
Per-tunnel and per-application performance across the WAN paths
explain: SD-WAN decisions depend on the latency, loss, and jitter of each tunnel and on the experience of each application, so monitoring must track both. Watching only device up/down status would hide the path degradation SD-WAN is meant to route around.

q: What is the role of a reverse proxy in a web architecture?
options: It sits in front of servers and forwards client requests to them
It sits on client devices and forwards their outbound requests
It assigns DHCP addresses to the servers behind a load balancer
It translates the private addresses of web servers using NAT
explain: A reverse proxy represents the servers to clients, receiving requests and passing them to the back end, which enables load balancing, caching, and shielding of the real servers. A forward proxy performs the mirror-image role on behalf of clients.

q: What does a forward proxy server do for client devices?
options: It forwards client requests to external resources on the clients' behalf
It assigns IP addresses to clients when they join the network
It routes packets between the local subnets at Layer 3
It blocks all outbound traffic generated by client devices
explain: A forward proxy makes requests to the Internet on behalf of internal clients, which allows the organization to cache content, filter destinations, and log outbound activity. Clients are configured, explicitly or transparently, to send their requests through it.

q: Why do geostationary satellite links, with round-trip latency around 600 ms, often require special optimization?
options: Because the latency is too low for TCP congestion control to work
Because satellite links are incapable of carrying encrypted traffic
Because satellite links are designed to carry only UDP traffic
Because the high delay degrades TCP performance and may require performance-enhancing proxies
explain: TCP throughput and connection setup suffer over very long delays, because acknowledgements and window growth take so long to return. Performance-enhancing proxies and other optimization techniques mitigate those effects on satellite paths.

q: Why is documenting the resolution an essential final step of troubleshooting?
options: It allows the team to delete the logs collected during the incident
It closes the loop so the next similar incident can be resolved faster
It transfers responsibility for the fix to the equipment vendor
It removes the need to test whether the implemented fix worked
explain: A written record of the cause and the fix becomes searchable knowledge for the next engineer who meets the same symptoms. Without it, the organization pays to rediscover the same solution on every recurrence.

q: What does Anycast Rendezvous Point (Anycast RP) provide in a PIM sparse-mode multicast network?
options: A method of assigning unicast addresses to multicast sources
A DNS-based method of selecting which multicast source to use
A single rendezvous point manually configured on one router only
Redundancy for the rendezvous point by sharing one RP address among several routers
explain: With Anycast RP, multiple routers advertise the same RP address, and sources and receivers use the nearest one, so the failure of one router does not remove the rendezvous point. It removes the single point of failure of a lone RP in PIM-SM.

q: What is a protocol analyzer such as Wireshark used for?
options: To decode captured packets in detail for troubleshooting
To block unwanted traffic according to firewall rule sets
To forward packets between two different IP networks
To assign addresses and prevent IP address conflicts
explain: A protocol analyzer captures frames and decodes each header and field, showing exactly what was sent, in what order, and with what timing. That visibility makes it a primary tool for diagnosing protocol and application faults.

q: Why is hiding the SSID not an effective primary security control for a wireless network?
options: Because a hidden network prevents legitimate clients from ever connecting
Because the SSID can still be discovered, so determined attackers are not stopped
Because hiding the SSID provides strong encryption for wireless traffic
Because hiding the SSID requires every client to connect using WPA3
explain: A hidden SSID still appears in probe requests and can be captured by anyone listening, so it adds no real protection. Strong encryption and authentication, such as WPA3 or WPA2 with 802.1X, are the controls that actually protect the network.

q: What is a hybrid network topology?
options: A topology that combines two or more topology types, such as star and bus
A topology in which all devices connect to one central switch only
A topology in which devices are arranged in a single closed loop only
A topology in which every device connects directly to every other device
explain: Real networks routinely mix topologies, for example a star of workstations attached to a bus or ring backbone, and that combination is a hybrid topology. Pure star, ring, and full mesh layouts are the individual types being combined.

q: What is a time domain reflectometer (TDR) used for?
options: To measure the strength of wireless signals inside a building
To locate opens and shorts in copper cabling and estimate the distance to the fault
To measure optical power loss along a fiber optic cable run
To measure the actual data throughput achieved between two endpoints
explain: A TDR sends a pulse down a copper cable and times the reflection from a fault, which locates opens and shorts and gives their distance from the tester. The fiber equivalent instrument is the OTDR, which works with light instead.

q: What kind of data does encryption at rest protect?
options: Data while it is being transmitted across a network link
Data stored on disks, databases, or backup media
Data while it is being processed in a processor's memory
Data after it has been displayed on a user's screen
explain: Encryption at rest, such as full-disk and database encryption, protects stored data if media are stolen, lost, or improperly disposed of. Data moving across a network is instead protected by encryption in transit, such as TLS or IPsec.

q: What is the primary function of a modem?
options: To route packets between two different IP networks
To switch frames between devices on a local network
To modulate and demodulate signals between digital devices and a carrier line
To amplify wireless signals in order to extend their coverage
explain: A modem converts a device's digital signals into the form required by a carrier technology such as DSL or cable, and converts incoming signals back again. Routing and switching are separate functions performed by routers and switches.

q: Which prefix identifies IPv6 multicast addresses?
explain: All IPv6 multicast addresses fall inside ff00::/8, and the well-known all-nodes group is ff02::1. By contrast, fe80::/10 is link-local unicast space, and IPv6 has no broadcast address because multicast takes over that role.

q: What causes a path MTU discovery black hole?
options: DNS responses that are larger than the maximum packet size
ICMP messages needed for path MTU discovery being blocked along the path
TCP connections that use a window size larger than the receiver expects
Routers that advertise an incorrect default gateway to their hosts
explain: Path MTU discovery relies on ICMP 'packet too big' messages to tell a sender to reduce its packet size. If a firewall blocks those messages, large packets are silently dropped and connections stall, which is fixed by allowing the ICMP messages or clamping the MSS.

q: What is the difference between a primary and a secondary DNS server for a zone?
options: Both servers hold writable copies that administrators edit independently
Both servers perform identical roles with no replication between them
The primary holds the writable zone, and secondaries copy it using zone transfers
The secondary server is where administrators should edit zone records
explain: Zone records are edited only on the primary server, and secondaries obtain their copies through zone transfers (AXFR or incremental IXFR). Running secondaries provides redundancy so name resolution survives the loss of the primary.

q: What does a DDoS scrubbing center do with traffic during a large attack?
options: It stores backup copies of the website for use while offline
It filters out the attack traffic and returns the clean traffic to the target
It permanently redirects all traffic to a different service provider
It encrypts the traffic so attackers can no longer see the target
explain: During an attack, traffic is diverted through a scrubbing center with enough capacity to absorb it, malicious traffic is discarded, and legitimate traffic is forwarded on to the target. This keeps the service available without the target's own links being saturated.

q: What was a CSU/DSU used for in a traditional WAN?
options: To connect a router to a digital WAN line such as a T1 circuit
To connect wireless clients to an enterprise wireless LAN
To switch Ethernet frames between devices on a local network
To provide routing between VLANs within a campus LAN
explain: A channel service unit/data service unit terminated digital carrier circuits such as T1 lines, handling framing, timing, and line diagnostics between the carrier and the customer's router. The function is now often built into router interface cards.

q: Why would an administrator place a device into maintenance mode in a monitoring system?
options: To suppress the expected alerts generated during a planned maintenance window
To permanently delete all monitoring checks configured for that device
To increase the sensitivity of alerting while the maintenance is performed
To allow the device to bypass the change management approval process
explain: Planned work predictably triggers alerts, and maintenance mode silences that expected noise for the duration of the window. Real problems on other systems then still stand out, and normal alerting resumes automatically afterward.

q: Why are 110-style punchdown blocks preferred over 66 blocks for modern data cabling?
options: 110 blocks support the higher frequencies data requires, while 66 blocks were designed mainly for voice
66 blocks were designed specifically for terminating fiber optic cabling
110 blocks are used to distribute electrical power within a wiring closet
66 blocks deliver better performance than 110 blocks for Gigabit Ethernet
explain: The older 66 block was designed for analog voice and does not meet the electrical requirements of Category-rated data cabling. The 110 block maintains the pair twist and supports the frequencies needed for Ethernet, so it is the standard for data terminations.

q: How does an Ethernet hub handle traffic it receives on one port?
options: It forwards each frame only to the port of the destination host
It selects a forwarding path using its IP routing table
It converts the signal between analog and digital forms
It repeats all incoming traffic out to every other port at Layer 1
explain: A hub is a Layer 1 repeater with no intelligence: every bit arriving on one port is regenerated out of all the others, so all attached devices share one collision domain and half-duplex operation. Switches replaced hubs because they forward frames only where they are needed.

q: How does anomaly-based intrusion detection identify potential threats?
options: It learns a baseline of normal behavior and flags deviations from that baseline
It matches traffic only against a database of known attack signatures
It blocks every flow that has not been explicitly permitted in advance
It applies a fixed rule set that never adapts to changes in the environment
explain: Anomaly detection builds a model of normal traffic and user behavior, then alerts on activity that departs from it, which can expose novel attacks that no signature exists for. Signature-based detection, by contrast, can only recognize patterns it already knows.

q: What is throughput on a network link?
options: The theoretical maximum capacity that the link is rated for
The size of the largest packet the link is able to carry
The actual rate at which data is successfully transferred
The time a packet takes to travel from source to destination
explain: Throughput is the real transfer rate achieved after protocol overhead, congestion, and errors are taken into account, so it is always at or below the link's rated bandwidth. Latency is the separate measurement of how long a packet takes to arrive.

q: What does network functions virtualization (NFV) do?
options: It requires a dedicated hardware appliance for each network function
It converts physical access switches into wireless access points
It runs network functions such as firewalls and routers as software on virtual infrastructure
It virtualizes user desktops and applications for remote access working
explain: NFV implements functions that used to need proprietary appliances, such as routers, firewalls, and load balancers, as virtual machines or containers on standard servers. That allows them to be deployed, scaled, and moved with software instead of new hardware.

q: What is the purpose of a business impact analysis (BIA) in disaster recovery planning?
options: To prioritize systems for recovery based on their criticality to the business
To calculate the insurance premiums charged for network equipment
To assign incoming helpdesk tickets according to technician availability
To verify backup media by restoring a selection of random files
explain: A BIA identifies which business functions and systems matter most, and how much downtime and data loss each can tolerate, expressed through measures such as RTO and RPO. Recovery spending and sequencing are then focused where an outage would hurt the business most.

q: Which statement best describes the use of TFTP to transfer firmware images to network devices?
options: It is secure, because it encrypts files and authenticates every user
It is preferred, because its design guarantees reliable delivery of files
It is simple, but it provides no authentication or encryption and offers no delivery reliability
It is a mandatory protocol for firmware upgrades on all modern devices
explain: TFTP is a minimal UDP-based protocol with no login, no encryption, and no retransmission guarantees, which makes it convenient in controlled environments but risky elsewhere. SCP, SFTP, or HTTPS transfers are preferred where security and reliability matter.

q: What does a service-level agreement (SLA) define between a provider and a customer?
options: The technical steps engineers follow when troubleshooting an outage
The list price charged for each individual network service offered
The agreed service performance levels and the remedies if they are not met
The internal targets a support team aims for without any formal commitment
explain: An SLA records measurable commitments such as uptime percentages and response times, together with consequences such as service credits when they are missed. Internal targets without a customer commitment are operating-level goals, not an SLA.

q: Why must the network operations center (NOC) and security operations center (SOC) coordinate their handoffs during an incident such as a DDoS attack?
options: Because only managers in each center are permitted to share incident details
Because monitoring tools resolve network and security issues automatically
Because both centers are responsible for performing one identical function
Because such events affect both operations and security, and responders need shared context
explain: A DDoS attack is simultaneously an availability problem for the NOC and a security event for the SOC, so both teams need the same timeline and findings to respond coherently. Coordinated handoffs prevent duplicated work and gaps in the response.

q: What does the Session layer (Layer 5) of the OSI model manage?
options: Framing and MAC addressing used for delivery on the local link
Transmission of raw bits across the physical network medium
Routing of packets between networks using logical IP addresses
Dialog control and the management of sessions between applications
explain: Layer 5 establishes, coordinates, and terminates conversations between applications, including dialog control and synchronization, as used by protocols such as NetBIOS and RPC. Addressing, routing, and bit transmission belong to Layers 2, 3, and 1 respectively.

q: Why is labeling cables and switch ports an important operational practice?
options: It significantly speeds up tracing connections during troubleshooting
It ensures that every cable in the plant uses one identical color
It replaces the need to maintain accurate network documentation
It improves the electrical performance of the cabling it is attached to
explain: Clearly labeled cables and ports turn tracing a connection from a lengthy physical hunt into a quick lookup, which shortens outages and reduces errors during changes. Labels support documentation rather than replacing it, and they have no effect on electrical performance.

q: What does an email security gateway primarily protect against?
options: It routes web browsing traffic through a proxy for content filtering
It filters incoming email for spam, phishing, and malware
It provides stateful firewall protection at the network perimeter
It manages the passwords users need to access their mailboxes
explain: An email security gateway inspects mail before delivery and blocks spam, phishing, and malicious attachments, often adding URL rewriting and attachment sandboxing. Those controls target business email compromise and credential phishing that a perimeter firewall cannot see.

q: Which symptom pattern most strongly suggests an MTU mismatch or path MTU black hole?
options: Large transfers fail or stall while small ping requests succeed
All DNS lookups fail while ordinary file transfers succeed
Every device on a network segment loses connectivity at the same time
Wireless clients roam repeatedly between neighboring access points
explain: Small packets fit under every MTU on the path, so pings succeed, but full-size packets for bulk transfers exceed a tunnel or link MTU and are dropped when fragmentation feedback is blocked. That size-dependent behavior is the classic signature of an MTU problem.

q: What is the purpose of a tabletop exercise for an operations team?
options: To test production hardware by deliberately causing a real outage
To rehearse the response to outage scenarios through a discussion-based walkthrough
To train only the security team in digital forensic analysis techniques
To document the final root cause after a real incident has ended
explain: A tabletop exercise talks the team through a scenario, such as a core switch failing overnight, to expose gaps in procedures, contacts, and decision-making. Because nothing is actually taken offline, the gaps can be found and fixed without any service risk.

q: What was Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP), and what is its status today?
options: An obsolete protocol that allowed a device to learn its IP address from its MAC address
The current protocol that resolves an IP address to a MAC address
The current protocol that assigns IP addresses together with gateway and DNS options
A wireless protocol that resolves hostnames to their IP addresses
explain: RARP let a diskless device broadcast its MAC address and receive back an IP address, but it supplied nothing else, so it was superseded by BOOTP and then DHCP. Resolving an IP address to a MAC address is the job of ordinary ARP, which is still in use.

q: What is the purpose of a Power over Ethernet (PoE) injector on a network link?
options: To provide switching between multiple Ethernet segments
To convert a fiber link to a copper link
To assign IP addresses to connected devices
To add electrical power to a data cable coming from a non-PoE switch
explain: A PoE injector sits between a non-PoE switch and a powered device such as an access point, adding power to the cable while passing data through unchanged.

q: What does a data loss prevention (DLP) system primarily do?
options: It creates and restores backups of sensitive files
It scans endpoints for malware and viruses
It detects and blocks the unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive data
It encrypts all data stored on a file server
explain: DLP inspects data in motion, in use, and at rest for sensitive content such as PCI, PHI, and PII, and can block it from leaving the organization. Antivirus and backup are separate functions.

q: What do private VLANs (PVLANs) allow an administrator to do?
options: Assign public IP addresses inside a private network
Isolate ports from each other even though they share the same VLAN
Trunk multiple VLANs over a single link
Route traffic between different VLANs without a router
explain: Private VLANs subdivide a VLAN so isolated ports cannot talk directly to each other, which is useful for guest or multi-tenant isolation, while still sharing a common gateway.

q: Why do modern data-center fabrics prefer a spine-leaf architecture?
options: Because it uses a single ring to connect all servers
Because it scales well and provides predictable, non-blocking connectivity
Because it requires fewer switches than a three-tier design in all cases
Because it eliminates the need for any Layer 3 routing
explain: In spine-leaf, every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, giving scalable, low-latency, any-to-any connectivity that suits heavy east-west server traffic better than a traditional three-tier design.

q: According to the longest prefix match rule, how does a router choose between two routes that both match a destination?
options: It selects the route that was learned first
It selects the route with the most specific (longest) matching prefix
It selects the route with the shortest prefix
It selects a route at random from the matching entries
explain: The router prefers the most specific match, so a /26 route beats a /24 route for the same destination because the /26 matches more bits of the address.

q: What does a DHCP scope define on a DHCP server?
options: The VLANs that are allowed on a trunk link
The static routes the server will advertise
The DNS zones the server is authoritative for
The pool of IP addresses available to lease to clients, along with its options
explain: A scope defines the leasable address range for a subnet, plus exclusions, reservations, lease duration, and options such as the default gateway and DNS servers.

q: What is the role of the default gateway in an IP host's configuration?
options: It routes traffic destined for networks outside the local subnet
It translates private IP addresses to public IP addresses
It resolves hostnames to IP addresses
It assigns IP addresses to hosts automatically
explain: A host sends packets for non-local destinations to its default gateway, which is a router interface on the local subnet. DNS resolves names and DHCP assigns addresses; neither routes traffic.

q: How many usable hosts in 10.0.0.0/22?
Users at one branch site report slow performance while all other sites are working normally. What should you check first?
options: The core switches at the headquarters site
The WAN link and uplink utilization and errors at the affected site
The DNS records for the affected site's servers
The firmware version on every switch in the organization
explain: When only one site is affected, the fault is most likely local to that site, so compare its WAN link and uplink utilization and error counters against healthy sites before investigating shared infrastructure.

q: What is a key characteristic of a spine-leaf architecture?
options: It is designed primarily for wide area network links
It provides predictable, low-latency connectivity well suited to east-west data-center traffic
It forwards traffic more slowly than a three-tier architecture by design
It is another name for the traditional three-tier architecture
explain: Every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, so any server can reach any other in a predictable number of hops with low latency, which suits east-west traffic.

q: How does cut-through switching forward a frame?
options: It stores the entire frame and verifies the FCS before forwarding
It forwards the frame only after buffering it for error checking
It converts the frame to a different media type before forwarding
It begins forwarding as soon as it has read the destination MAC address
explain: Cut-through switches start forwarding after reading the destination MAC, giving very low latency. The trade-off is that corrupted frames can be propagated because the FCS is not checked first, unlike store-and-forward switching.

q: What distinguishes out-of-band management from in-band management?
options: It manages devices using the same production network as user traffic
It manages devices without using any network connection at all
It uses a separate, dedicated network for device administration
It manages devices exclusively through the Telnet protocol
explain: Out-of-band management uses a dedicated management network, often a separate VLAN or physical network, so administrators can reach devices even when production traffic paths are down or compromised.

q: Why should an administrator monitor CPU and memory utilization on network devices?
options: To catch overload conditions before they cause device failure
To measure the throughput of individual user sessions
To replace the need for interface error monitoring
To determine which VLANs are carrying the most traffic
explain: Sustained high CPU or memory use on a router or switch can degrade the control plane and cause routing or forwarding problems, so trending these values gives early warning before a failure.

q: What is the most common cause of a broadcast storm on a switched network?
options: A switching loop that repeatedly forwards broadcast frames
An oversubscribed but loop-free uplink
A router advertising a default route
Assigning hosts to multiple VLANs
explain: Without loop prevention, a switching loop causes broadcast frames to multiply exponentially until the network saturates. Spanning Tree Protocol exists specifically to prevent these loops.

q: What is an OTDR used to test?
options: Wireless signal strength and channel interference
Copper cable length and wiremap faults
The location of fiber breaks and bad splices along a fiber run
The actual throughput between two network devices
explain: An Optical Time-Domain Reflectometer sends light pulses down a fiber and measures reflections to map splices, connectors, and faults by distance.

q: What problem does active queue management such as FQ-CoDel address?
options: It controls bufferbloat by using fair queuing and early packet drops to keep latency low
It guarantees bandwidth to a single priority flow
It replaces fair queuing with strict first-in, first-out handling
It eliminates the need for any packet buffering
explain: FQ-CoDel combines fair queuing with controlled-delay drops, so large buffers do not fill up and add latency under load — the bufferbloat problem that plain FIFO queuing makes worse.

q: What is the main improvement of SNMPv3 over SNMPv2c?
options: It uses simpler community strings than SNMPv2c
It adds authentication and encryption for management traffic
It provides a larger set of MIB objects than SNMPv2c
It polls devices significantly faster than SNMPv2c
explain: SNMPv3 adds user-based authentication and optional encryption (authPriv), fixing SNMPv2c's weakness of sending community strings in cleartext.

q: What happens when single-mode fiber is connected to a multimode transceiver (optic)?
options: The optics negotiate a common mode automatically and the link runs at the lower rate
The link works if both connectors use the same polish type
The link comes up but with a higher bit error rate only
The link will not come up because of the wavelength and mode mismatch
explain: Single-mode and multimode optics use different core sizes and wavelengths, so mixing fiber type and optic type prevents a proper link. Always match the optic to the installed fiber plant.

q: What does the R-factor measure in a VoIP network?
options: The redundancy level of a voice gateway
It estimates voice call quality on a scale of 0 to 100
The number of simultaneous calls a firewall can inspect
The resolution and frame rate of a video call
explain: The R-factor (R-value) is a calculated score from 0 to 100 that estimates perceived call quality and maps to a Mean Opinion Score (MOS), making it useful for tracking quality trends per call.

q: Which of the following is part of properly hardening SSH access on a network device?
options: Allowing Telnet as a fallback if SSH fails
Permitting SSH version 2 only, using strong ciphers, and restricting access with ACLs
Removing all ACLs so administrators can connect from anywhere
Enabling SSH version 1 for compatibility with older clients
explain: SSH hardening means using version 2 only, strong ciphers, key-based authentication where possible, and an access list limiting which hosts may connect. SSHv1 and Telnet fallback both undermine that security.

q: Why should a technician document the resolution of a network problem?
options: It builds a knowledge base that speeds up future troubleshooting
It satisfies a requirement to log every packet on the network
It replaces the need to verify that the fix worked
It allows the ticket to be closed without testing the solution
explain: Documenting symptoms, cause, and resolution creates a knowledge base entry that helps resolve similar incidents faster in the future.

q: Why should an organization keep a spare parts inventory for network hardware?
options: To avoid ever having to open a support contract with a vendor
To store equipment that will be installed in a future project
To speed up hardware replacement when a component fails
To increase the resale value of retired equipment
explain: Keeping critical spares such as power supplies, fans, and optics on hand shortens repair time because a failed part can be swapped immediately instead of waiting for a shipment.

q: At which layer of the OSI model are IP addresses defined?
options: Layer 4, the Transport layer
Layer 2, the Data Link layer
Layer 3, the Network layer
Layer 1, the Physical layer
explain: IP provides logical addressing and routing at Layer 3, the Network layer. MAC addresses operate at Layer 2, and ports operate at Layer 4.

q: What does TCP congestion control primarily prevent?
options: Bit errors on the physical media
Senders overwhelming the network with more traffic than it can carry
Routing loops between autonomous systems
A receiver being overwhelmed by data it cannot process in time
explain: Congestion control, using slow start and congestion avoidance, adapts the sending rate to network capacity to avoid overwhelming intermediate links. Preventing receiver overload is flow control, handled by the receive window.

q: What is the purpose of a DNS SRV record?
options: To map a hostname to an IPv4 address
To locate services by type, such as LDAP or SIP, including port and priority
To create an alias from one hostname to another
To specify the mail servers for a domain
explain: SRV records advertise where a specific service can be reached, including hostname, port, priority, and weight — for example for LDAP or SIP. A records map names to IPv4 addresses and CNAMEs create aliases.

q: How are devices connected in a bus topology?
options: All devices share a single backbone cable
All devices connect to a central switch
Each device connects to two neighboring devices in a ring
Each device has a dedicated point-to-point link to every other device
explain: In a bus topology, used by legacy coaxial Ethernet, all devices attach to one shared backbone cable, so a break or terminator fault can take down the whole segment.

q: Why should an organization regularly test its disaster recovery plan?
options: To satisfy auditors without changing any procedures
To confirm that backups exist on paper
To reduce the number of backups that must be stored
To validate that failover actually works when it is needed
explain: Untested disaster recovery plans often fail during a real event. Regular testing exercises failover and exposes gaps while there is still time to fix them.

q: What is MAC authentication bypass (MAB) used for in a network access control deployment?
options: It performs full 802.1X authentication using certificates
It encrypts traffic for devices that do not support 802.1X
It authenticates devices by their MAC address when they cannot run 802.1X
It blocks devices whose MAC address is not on an allow list
explain: MAB lets devices such as printers and IoT hardware that lack an 802.1X supplicant be authenticated by MAC address instead. It is weaker than 802.1X, so it is often paired with device profiling.

q: What is the purpose of an incident bridge during a major network outage?
options: To provide a physical backup link between two sites
To record all traffic passing through the core switch
To replace the formal incident ticket for the outage
To coordinate responders and communication during a major incident
explain: An incident bridge, often a virtual war room, brings the responding teams together on one call or channel so work and status updates stay coordinated during a high-priority incident.

q: A trunk link between two switches is missing a VLAN from its allowed VLAN list. What is the effect?
options: That VLAN's traffic is forwarded untagged instead
All VLANs are allowed until the list is corrected
Traffic for that VLAN is blocked from crossing the trunk
The trunk negotiates a faster speed to compensate
explain: A trunk only carries VLANs in its allowed list, so a missing VLAN cannot pass traffic across that link. Check the allowed VLAN configuration on both ends of the trunk.

q: What does a risk assessment identify during network security planning?
options: The cable types used in each wiring closet
The usernames of all employees with network access
Only the external attackers most likely to target the network
The threats, vulnerabilities, and potential impacts facing the organization
explain: A risk assessment maps what can go wrong — threats exploiting vulnerabilities — and how severe the impact would be, so controls can be chosen in proportion to the risk.

q: Which prefix is reserved for use in IPv6 documentation and examples?
explain: 2001:db8::/32 is reserved for documentation and examples and is never routed on the public Internet. fe80::/10 is link-local and fc00::/7 is unique local addressing.

q: What best describes the geographic scope of a WAN?
options: Connections between devices within a single desk or work area
Connections between devices within a single room or office
Connections between devices within a single building
Connections spanning large geographic areas, such as cities or countries
explain: A wide area network connects sites across large distances, typically using carrier links, whereas a LAN stays within a local area such as a building.

q: What does secure (pull) printing require before a document is printed?
options: The document is printed immediately so the tray stays clear
The printer is left open for any user on the network
The job is sent to every printer in the building
The user authenticates at the printer, for example with a badge, to release the job
explain: Secure or pull printing holds the job until the owner authenticates at the device, preventing sensitive documents from sitting unattended in the output tray.

q: What does the storm control feature on a switch do?
options: It rate-limits broadcast, multicast, or unknown unicast floods on a port
It prioritizes voice traffic over data traffic
It blocks all traffic during a spanning-tree reconvergence
It extends VLANs across a wide area link
explain: Storm control caps flood traffic at a configured percentage of bandwidth on a port, limiting the damage from loops or malfunctioning devices.

q: How does deception technology help detect attackers?
options: It lies to legitimate users about the location of real shares
It plants fake credentials, shares, and systems that lure attackers into monitored traps
It encrypts all real credentials so they cannot be stolen
It blocks attackers at the perimeter before they can connect
explain: Deception technology seeds believable decoys — fake credentials, shares, and hosts — so any interaction with them is a high-confidence sign of malicious activity.

q: How is a TCP connection normally torn down gracefully?
options: By sending a single RST segment from either side
By stopping transmission with no notification to the peer
By flooding the peer with SYN segments
Through FIN and ACK exchanges in both directions
explain: A graceful close uses FIN/ACK exchanges so each side confirms it has finished sending. An RST, by contrast, aborts a connection abruptly.

q: What do the Nyquist and Shannon theorems describe?
options: How IP address classes are allocated
The standard pinout for Ethernet cabling
The port numbers assigned to common services
The maximum data rate achievable over a channel given its bandwidth and noise
explain: Nyquist and Shannon bound channel capacity: capacity depends on available bandwidth and the signal-to-noise ratio, which is why noise limits real-world throughput.

q: What does the MTR tool combine into a single continuous diagnostic?
options: Email delivery testing and web page loading
DNS lookups and DHCP lease information
ARP table inspection and a single ping
Ping and traceroute, showing per-hop loss and latency over time
explain: MTR (My Traceroute) continuously combines ping and traceroute, reporting loss and latency for every hop, which makes it well suited to intermittent path problems.

q: A patch cord has a bent and damaged boot that strains its termination. What should you do?
options: Compress the boot with a heat gun to restore its shape
Replace the cord because the strain can damage the termination
Straighten the boot and cover it with tape
Move the cord to a less important device and monitor it
explain: Boots protect the plug from sharp bends and strain. A damaged boot lets the cable stress the termination, causing intermittent faults, so the cord should be replaced.

q: A branch router's LTE backup connection has a consistently weak signal. What is the best remedy?
options: Reduce the router's LTE polling interval to conserve the weak signal
Reposition the antenna or install an external antenna or booster
Switch the router to use Wi-Fi as its WAN connection
Increase the transmit power setting on the LAN switch
explain: Marginal cellular service is usually a placement problem; relocating the antenna, using an external antenna, or adding a booster improves signal strength and stability.

q: Two network events occur at the same time. Why should a technician be careful about correlation versus causation here?
options: Because the events must be verified before concluding that one caused the other
Because simultaneous events are always caused by the same fault
Because timing information is never useful in troubleshooting
Because the correct response is always to act on both events immediately
explain: Events happening together may be coincidence rather than cause and effect. Verify the relationship with evidence before acting, or you may fix the wrong thing.

q: Which type of probe does the Windows tracert utility use by default?
options: ARP requests
UDP probes to high ports
ICMP echo requests
TCP SYN segments
explain: Windows tracert sends ICMP echo requests with increasing TTL values. Linux traceroute, by contrast, defaults to UDP probes.

q: How does ICMP rate limiting help protect a network?
options: By disabling ping on all internal hosts
By encrypting ICMP traffic between routers
By applying TCP congestion control to ICMP flows
By blunting ICMP-based floods such as smurf and ping floods
explain: Rate-limiting ICMP, together with disabling directed broadcasts, reduces the effectiveness of smurf and ping flood attacks that abuse ICMP echo traffic.

q: What is the role of a network operations center (NOC)?
options: To investigate security incidents as a security operations center would
To centrally monitor network health and performance, typically 24/7
To approve all changes before they are implemented
To provide help desk support for end-user devices only
explain: A NOC centrally monitors network health and performance around the clock. A SOC is a separate function focused on security monitoring and incidents.

q: What does forward error correction (FEC) allow a receiver to do?
options: Request a retransmission of every lost packet
Encrypt data so errors cannot be introduced in transit
Compress data so fewer packets need to be sent
Recover lost or corrupted data without retransmission, using added redundant data
explain: FEC adds redundancy that lets the receiver reconstruct lost data without a round-trip retransmission, which is valuable on high-latency lossy links such as satellite connections.

q: In bottom-up troubleshooting, at which OSI layer do you start?
options: Layer 3, the Network layer
Layer 7, the Application layer
Layer 2, the Data Link layer
Layer 1, the Physical layer
explain: Bottom-up troubleshooting starts at the Physical layer — cables, connectors, and link lights — and works up the stack from there.

q: What characterizes in-band management of a network device?
options: It encrypts all management traffic by default
It requires no IP connectivity to the device
It uses a physically separate network from production traffic
It shares the production network paths used by regular traffic
explain: In-band management traffic travels over the production network, which is convenient but exposes management interfaces to production threats and to production outages.

q: What is the most effective way to reduce alert fatigue in a monitoring system?
options: Tuning thresholds and deduplicating alerts so only actionable events notify
Making alert notifications louder and more frequent
Training staff to ignore low-priority alerts
Generating more alerts so no event is ever missed
explain: Alert fatigue falls when thresholds are tuned and duplicate alerts are suppressed, so every notification that reaches a human requires action.

q: What is the function of a VXLAN tunnel endpoint (VTEP)?
options: To route traffic between physical data centers only
To assign VLAN IDs to physical switch ports
To terminate physical fiber connections from servers
To encapsulate and decapsulate VXLAN overlay traffic at the edge of the underlay
explain: VTEPs are the tunnel endpoints that map tenant segments (VNIs) to the overlay and encapsulate and decapsulate frames as they enter and leave the VXLAN tunnel.

q: What does media sanitization involve before a storage device is disposed of?
options: Deleting the files and emptying the recycle bin
Formatting the drive with a quick format
Wiping, degaussing, or physically destroying the media according to its classification
Encrypting the drive and discarding the key in the same shipment
explain: Sanitization uses a method matched to the data's classification — clearing, purging such as degaussing, or destruction — and verifies it. Simple deletion leaves data recoverable.

q: What defines top-of-rack (ToR) switching in a data center?
options: Switches are centralized at the end of each row of racks
A switch is placed in each rack, connecting that rack's servers
Servers connect through hubs located under the raised floor
Each rack uses a single switch shared with all other racks
explain: Top-of-rack design puts one or two switches in every rack, keeping server cabling short. End-of-row design, by contrast, centralizes switches at the row's end.

q: What is the maximum channel length for a horizontal Ethernet copper run?
options: 100 meters
10 meters
500 meters
185 meters
explain: The Ethernet copper channel is limited to 100 meters, typically 90 meters of solid horizontal cable plus up to 10 meters of patch cords. Longer runs require fiber or an extender.

q: Why is port mirroring commonly used to feed an intrusion detection system (IDS)?
options: It lets the IDS block traffic without affecting the live flow
It feeds the IDS a copy of traffic with no inline failure risk to production traffic
It places the IDS inline so it can drop malicious packets
It encrypts the copied traffic before the IDS inspects it
explain: A mirror (SPAN) port sends a copy of traffic to a passive IDS, so monitoring continues without the availability risk that an inline device failing would create.

q: What information does NetFlow analysis primarily reveal?
options: The passwords used in application sessions
The full payload contents of each packet
The encryption keys used on VPN tunnels
The top talkers and traffic patterns between hosts
explain: Flow records summarize who talked to whom, on which ports, and how much data moved — ideal for spotting top talkers and trends. NetFlow does not capture payloads or passwords.

q: How does NRZ (non-return-to-zero) encoding represent bits on a link?
options: As shifts in the phase of the signal
As discrete voltage levels held for the bit duration
As pulses of light only, with no electrical form
As shifts in the frequency of the signal
explain: NRZ holds one voltage level for a 1 and another for a 0 for the full bit period, rather than encoding bits as phase or frequency changes.

q: What does a switch's MAC address (CAM) table map?
options: IP addresses to MAC addresses
MAC addresses to the switch ports where they were learned
Hostnames to IP addresses
Network addresses to their best routing paths
explain: The CAM table records which source MAC address was seen on which port, so the switch can forward a frame only out the correct port. Mapping IPs to MACs is ARP's job.

q: What key efficiency features does 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6/6E) add over earlier Wi-Fi standards?
options: Higher peak data rates with no other changes
Support for WEP encryption for legacy clients
OFDMA and uplink MU-MIMO for better performance in dense environments
Operation only in the 6 GHz band
explain: 802.11ax focuses on efficiency and density, adding OFDMA, uplink MU-MIMO, and other features that improve real-world performance when many clients share a channel, not just peak rate.

q: What type of address mapping does static NAT provide?
options: A random public address chosen for each session
A many-to-one mapping of internal hosts to one public address
A one-to-one, permanent mapping between an internal and a public address
No mapping between internal and public addresses
explain: Static NAT permanently maps one inside address to one outside address, which suits servers that must be reachable at a consistent public IP. Many-to-one mapping describes PAT.

q: What is the purpose of a patch panel in structured cabling?
options: It terminates horizontal cabling so drops can be cross-connected with patch cords
It amplifies signals on long cable runs
It switches frames between connected devices
It routes packets between different networks
explain: A patch panel is a passive termination point for horizontal runs; short patch cords then connect panel ports to switch ports, keeping moves and changes orderly.

q: What is the purpose of DSL filters (microfilters) on a DSL line?
options: They are optional accessories that improve call quality only
They separate voice frequencies from DSL data frequencies on the shared line
They slow the DSL connection to protect voice calls
They convert the DSL signal for use by Ethernet devices
explain: DSL and voice share the line in different frequency bands. Filters keep telephones from injecting noise into the DSL band and keep DSL tones out of voice calls.

q: Two hosts that should be able to reach each other are placed in different VLANs by mistake. What symptom results?
options: DNS resolution fails for both hosts
A routing loop forms between the hosts
The hosts lose connectivity to each other because they are in different broadcast domains
Both hosts receive their addresses from the same DHCP scope
explain: Hosts in different VLANs are in separate broadcast domains and cannot reach each other without routing. Verify access VLAN assignments and trunk allowed lists when expected peers cannot connect.

q: What does a media converter do?
options: It routes packets between different IP networks
It switches frames between ports in the same network
It amplifies a signal to extend a copper run indefinitely
It joins different media types, such as converting between copper and fiber Ethernet
explain: A media converter bridges two Ethernet media types — for example UTP copper to fiber — at the physical layer, without routing or switching decisions.

q: What is required to route traffic between two different VLANs?
options: A router or a Layer 3 switch
