By replacing the customer's modem without testing the line
By checking the customer's Wi-Fi signal strength in each room
By assigning the customer a new static public IP address
explain: Moving the customer to a different DSLAM port or pair and retesting, including testing at the network interface device, separates a provider port fault from inside wiring or customer equipment.

q: How does router-on-a-stick provide inter-VLAN routing?
options: It uses a separate physical router interface for each VLAN
It uses a wireless controller to route traffic between VLANs
It uses subinterfaces on a single physical link trunked to a switch, one per VLAN
It uses multiple routers connected in a redundant ring
explain: Router-on-a-stick uses one physical router interface connected by a trunk to a switch. Each VLAN gets its own subinterface on that link, which acts as its default gateway.

q: What should be done about corroded electrical contacts on a network connection?
options: Leave them in place, as corrosion improves conductivity over time
Coat them with insulating grease and reconnect them without cleaning
Clean them with an approved contact cleaner or replace the affected connector
Increase transmit power to compensate for the added resistance
explain: Corrosion adds resistance and causes intermittent faults. Cleaning the contacts with an approved cleaner, reseating the connection, or replacing the connector restores a reliable path.

q: How is bandwidth best defined?
options: The amount of data actually transferred during a test, measured over time
The variation in delay experienced by packets in a flow
The time it takes for a single packet to travel from source to destination
The theoretical maximum data rate a link can carry
explain: Bandwidth is the capacity of a link — its theoretical maximum rate. Throughput is the actual rate achieved, which is affected by latency (delay) and jitter (variation in delay).

q: Which two modes can IPsec operate in?
options: Aggressive mode and main mode only
Transport mode and tunnel mode
Encrypted mode and clear-text mode
Client mode and server mode only
explain: In transport mode IPsec protects only the payload, typically between hosts. In tunnel mode it encrypts the entire original IP packet and adds a new header, which is how site-to-site VPNs usually work.

q: What is the primary function of a wireless access point (WAP)?
options: It bridges wireless clients onto the wired LAN
It inspects traffic and blocks malicious applications as a firewall
It assigns public IP addresses to all wireless clients
It routes traffic between two wide area networks
explain: An access point is primarily a Layer 2 bridge between 802.11 wireless clients and the 802.3 wired LAN. Routing, DHCP, and firewall functions are separate roles, even if combined in one consumer device.

q: Which practice is considered cable management best practice in a rack?
options: Organized, labeled cables with appropriate service loops and bend radius
Cables pulled tightly with sharp bends to save space in the rack
Unlabeled cables bundled together to reduce documentation work
Excess cable coiled tightly around power cables for neatness
explain: Neat, labeled cabling with service loops and proper bend radius improves airflow, protects cables from damage, and makes tracing and troubleshooting much faster.

q: What is the purpose of a shared maintenance calendar?
options: To schedule employee vacations and on-call rotations only
To record the warranty expiration dates of network hardware
To document the results of completed network changes
To coordinate planned changes and maintenance windows to avoid conflicts
explain: A maintenance calendar makes planned work visible to all teams, preventing overlapping disruptive changes and scheduling conflicts.

q: What does Power over Ethernet (PoE) testing verify?
options: That a cable meets its Category rating for data transmission speed
That power is delivered correctly over the cable pairs at the required wattage
That an end device has obtained a valid IP address via DHCP
That a switch port is configured for the correct VLAN
explain: PoE testing checks that the powered device is correctly classified and receives the required voltage and wattage under load. Data speed and VLAN tests check different properties.

q: Two VPN sites both use 192.168.1.0/24 for their LANs. How can the VPN be made to work between them?
options: Enable split tunneling on both VPN gateways
Increase the tunnel MTU on both gateways
Use the same default gateway address at both sites
Use NAT to translate one or both networks, or readdress one of the sites
explain: Identical subnets at both ends cannot be routed unambiguously across a tunnel. Translating the overlapping addresses with NAT, or renumbering one site, resolves the conflict.

q: Why is network segmentation important for operational technology (OT) environments?
options: It allows OT devices to share a flat network with office workstations
It enables IT systems to directly manage all industrial controllers
It isolates industrial control systems from IT networks and limits exposure to threats
It replaces the need for firewalls between plant floor levels
explain: Segmentation, as in the Purdue model, separates OT levels with controlled conduits between them. This limits the ability of an IT-side compromise to reach industrial control systems.

q: In a passive optical network (PON), what effect does a split ratio such as 1:32 have?
options: It determines the maximum cable distance for each subscriber only
It applies only to copper-based access networks, not fiber
It shares the downstream bandwidth among 32 subscribers, affecting per-user capacity
It guarantees each subscriber the full OLT port bandwidth at all times
explain: A 1:32 splitter shares one OLT port among 32 subscribers, so the available bandwidth is divided among them. Higher split ratios reduce per-user capacity, especially at peak times.

q: What is simplex communication?
options: Data flows in both directions, but only one direction at a time
Data flows in both directions simultaneously
Data flows in one direction only
Data flows only over an encrypted channel
explain: Simplex is one-way only, like a television broadcast. Half-duplex allows both directions but not at the same time, and full-duplex allows both directions simultaneously.

q: What is the most reliable way to confirm that a suspected component has failed?
options: Reboot the device and see if the symptom returns
Review vendor release notes for a matching known bug
Swap the suspect component with a known-good part and retest
Monitor the device for an additional day without making changes
explain: Substitution isolates the fault: if a known-good cable, module, or power supply fixes the problem, the original component is confirmed faulty.

q: Why does sFlow use sampling instead of capturing every packet?
options: It trades some precision for the ability to monitor high-speed links at scale
It is designed primarily for accurate per-packet billing
It captures complete packet payloads for detailed forensic analysis
It provides exact packet counts identical to a full packet capture
explain: sFlow samples a fraction of packets, such as 1 in 1000, which is enough to show traffic patterns on very large links without overwhelming the collector. It is less precise than full capture by design.

q: What does SSL/TLS inspection do?
options: It decrypts TLS traffic for security analysis, with privacy and compatibility trade-offs to consider
It encrypts traffic that was previously sent in clear text
It inspects only email traffic for malicious attachments
It bypasses certificate validation to speed up web browsing
explain: TLS inspection decrypts traffic at a security device so it can be analyzed, then re-encrypts it. This improves visibility but raises privacy concerns and can break applications that use certificate pinning.

q: What can happen if EtherChannel is configured on only one end of a link bundle?
options: The links will negotiate a higher speed automatically
Traffic will use only the first link and ignore the remaining links
Spanning-tree loops or traffic problems can occur because the ends disagree on bundling
The switch will convert the bundle to a routed port automatically
explain: Both ends must agree on the bundle, whether through LACP or static configuration. A mismatch can cause loops, blocked ports, or uneven and dropped traffic.

q: What does the Windows pathping command do?
options: It sends a single ping to measure round-trip time to a destination
It lists the IP configuration of all local network interfaces
It traces the route to a destination and then measures packet loss at each hop over time
It resolves a hostname to an IP address using DNS
explain: Pathping combines tracert and ping: it first discovers the route, then sends many pings to each hop to calculate loss and latency. This per-hop analysis pinpoints where loss occurs, but it takes time to complete.

q: How does WPA2-Personal authenticate wireless clients?
options: It requires each user to authenticate with a unique username via 802.1X
It uses a pre-shared key (PSK) shared by all clients on the network
It requires a client certificate installed on each device
It uses an open authentication method with no key or credentials
explain: WPA2-Personal uses a single pre-shared key for the network, which suits homes and small offices. WPA2-Enterprise instead uses 802.1X with individual user or device credentials.

q: In networking, what is a gateway?
options: A device that regenerates signals to extend a cable segment, like a hub
A device or service that translates between different protocols or networks
A Layer 2 device that forwards frames based on MAC addresses, like a switch
A device used only to assign IP addresses to hosts on a LAN
explain: A gateway connects dissimilar systems by translating protocols or formats, such as a protocol converter or application proxy. This is broader than a router, which forwards packets between IP networks.

q: What does tunneling IPv6 over IPv4 mean?
options: Translating IPv6 addresses into IPv4 addresses at a NAT gateway
Encapsulating IPv6 packets inside IPv4 packets for transport across an IPv4 network
Assigning IPv4 addresses to hosts that only support IPv6
Encrypting IPv4 packets using IPv6 security extensions
explain: Tunneling methods such as 6to4, Teredo, and configured tunnels carry IPv6 packets inside IPv4 packets. This lets IPv6 islands communicate across an IPv4-only path.

q: What does a private VLAN edge (protected port) feature do on a switch?
options: It allows a port to carry traffic for multiple VLANs as a trunk
It provides a routed connection between two different VLANs
It connects the switch to a WAN provider edge router
It prevents a port from communicating directly with other protected ports in the same VLAN
explain: Protected ports cannot send traffic directly to other protected ports in the same VLAN, though they can still reach unprotected ports such as the gateway. This isolates clients in places like hotels and dorms.

q: After implementing a fix, what must a technician do according to the troubleshooting methodology?
options: Close the ticket immediately once the change is applied
Verify full system functionality and implement measures to prevent recurrence
Document the original problem description from the ticket
Establish a theory of probable cause for the next incident
explain: After a solution is implemented, verify that the system is fully functional and, if applicable, implement preventive measures. Documentation follows verification.

q: How does SNMP polling work?
options: Devices send unsolicited alerts to a manager only when a threshold is crossed
A management station queries devices on a regular schedule to collect counters and status
Devices push a continuous stream of telemetry to a collector in real time
A management station logs in by SSH to run show commands on each device
explain: In SNMP polling, the manager periodically queries agents for values such as interface counters and CPU use. Unsolicited messages from a device are traps, not polling.

q: Where was CSMA/CD originally used?
options: On fiber-optic backbone links using full-duplex connections
On Wi-Fi networks using half-duplex radio channels
On legacy half-duplex Ethernet networks using hubs or shared media
On modern full-duplex switched Ethernet networks
explain: CSMA/CD detected collisions on shared, half-duplex Ethernet using hubs or coaxial media. Full-duplex switched Ethernet eliminated collisions, and Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CA instead.

q: What does a cost-per-ticket metric measure?
options: The efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the support operation
The salary cost of the senior engineer assigned to a ticket
The total hardware cost associated with resolving an outage
The price a customer pays for each support contract renewal
explain: Cost per ticket divides total support costs by the number of tickets handled, indicating operational efficiency. It should be tracked alongside quality so that cheaper does not mean worse service.

q: Why would an administrator run GRE over IPsec?
options: To increase the bandwidth of a GRE tunnel by compressing its traffic
To replace the need for routing protocols across a VPN tunnel
To allow GRE traffic to bypass all security inspection
To add IPsec encryption and authentication to traffic carried by a GRE tunnel
explain: GRE alone provides encapsulation, including support for multicast routing protocols, but no encryption. Adding IPsec protects the GRE traffic with encryption and authentication.

q: What is the purpose of a DNS reverse lookup zone?
options: It maps IP addresses to hostnames using PTR records in the in-addr.arpa domain
It maps hostnames to IP addresses using A and AAAA records
It delegates authority for a subdomain to another name server
It stores text records used for email authentication policies
explain: Reverse zones hold PTR records that resolve an IP address back to a hostname, under in-addr.arpa for IPv4. Forward zones hold A and AAAA records for name-to-address lookups.

q: Which symptoms most likely indicate a failing power supply in a network device?
options: Improved throughput and lower CPU utilization
A steady green status LED and no entries in the system log
Faster PoE negotiation with connected devices
Random reboots, unexpected shutdowns, or loss of PoE to connected devices
explain: A failing power supply often causes intermittent reboots, complete shutdowns, or loss of power to PoE devices. Checking PSU LEDs, logs, and any redundant supply helps confirm it.

q: What distinguishes a stateful firewall from a stateless packet filter?
options: It cannot perform Network Address Translation
It tracks the state of connections and allows return traffic for established sessions
It inspects only the destination port of each individual packet
It blocks all return traffic unless a separate rule is created for it
explain: A stateful firewall maintains a state table for connections and automatically permits legitimate return traffic. A stateless filter evaluates each packet in isolation against its rules.

q: How does EAP-TTLS differ from PEAP?
options: It requires a client-side certificate on every supplicant
It supports a wider range of inner authentication methods, including legacy methods such as PAP and CHAP
It does not use a TLS tunnel to protect the inner authentication
It is used only for wired 802.1X authentication, not wireless
explain: Both PEAP and EAP-TTLS establish a TLS tunnel and then run an inner authentication method inside it. TTLS supports more inner methods, including legacy PAP and CHAP, and does not require client certificates.

q: What does DKIM do for outgoing email?
options: It publishes a list of servers authorized to send mail for a domain
It defines how receivers should handle mail that fails authentication
It encrypts the contents of an email message for the recipient
It cryptographically signs outgoing messages so receivers can verify integrity and domain origin
explain: DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing mail, which receivers verify using a public key published in DNS. SPF (the authorized-sender list) and DMARC (the handling policy) are separate mechanisms.

q: A device has an MTBF of 50,000 hours. What does that mean?
options: It is guaranteed to fail at 50,000 hours
On average, it runs 50,000 hours between failures
It must be replaced at 50,000 hours
It lasts exactly 50,000 hours
explain: MTBF (mean time between failures) is a statistical average across many units, not a promise for one device. A single unit can fail much sooner or run far longer.

q: What is Manchester encoding used for?
options: To encrypt data before transmission over a shared medium
To compress data by removing redundant bit patterns
To embed clock information in the signal by using a transition in each bit period
To modulate data onto a wireless carrier frequency
explain: Manchester encoding guarantees a transition in the middle of each bit period, so the receiver can recover the clock from the signal itself. It was used in early Ethernet standards such as 10BASE-T.

q: What is the main trade-off to consider with TLS inspection?
options: Increased visibility into encrypted traffic versus privacy, performance, and application compatibility concerns
Improved network speed versus the cost of additional firewall hardware
Stronger encryption versus the need for larger certificate key sizes
Simpler compliance reporting versus the cost of log storage
explain: TLS inspection improves security visibility, but it decrypts private traffic, adds processing overhead, and can break applications that use certificate pinning. Those privacy and performance costs must be weighed before deployment.

q: How does a split-tunnel VPN differ from a full-tunnel VPN?
options: It requires no VPN connection for remote corporate access
It sends all remote user traffic through the corporate tunnel
It sends only corporate-destined traffic through the tunnel, while other traffic uses the local Internet connection
It tunnels traffic only when the user is connected to the office LAN
explain: Split tunneling sends only traffic destined for corporate resources through the VPN, saving bandwidth and allowing direct Internet access for other traffic. A full tunnel sends everything through the corporate gateway for inspection.

q: Why should NAT Traversal (NAT-T) be disabled on an IPsec VPN when no NAT device is in the path?
options: It adds unnecessary encapsulation overhead by wrapping ESP in UDP
It prevents the VPN tunnel from establishing a Phase 1 session
It forces the tunnel to use weaker encryption algorithms
It causes the tunnel to drop whenever the public IP address changes
explain: NAT-T encapsulates ESP inside UDP port 4500 so it can pass through NAT. When no NAT is present, that extra encapsulation is unnecessary overhead.

q: What does business service monitoring focus on?
options: The CPU and memory utilization of individual servers only
The number of support tickets opened for a department
The sales revenue generated by an online storefront
Whether user-facing services and business outcomes, such as completing a checkout, are working correctly
explain: Business service monitoring measures the end-user outcome — for example, whether customers can complete a checkout — rather than only whether individual servers are up. A service can fail even when every device appears healthy.

q: What does the EtherType field in an Ethernet frame identify?
options: The physical cable type used for the link
The MAC address of the sending device
The negotiated speed and duplex of the link
The upper-layer protocol carried in the frame, such as IPv4, ARP, or IPv6
explain: EtherType tells the receiver which protocol is in the payload: 0x0800 for IPv4, 0x0806 for ARP, and 0x86DD for IPv6.

q: Which email protocols use TCP ports 110 and 143 by default?
options: DNS on 110 and DHCP on 143
FTP on 110 and SSH on 143
POP3 on 110 and IMAP on 143
SMTP on 110 and HTTP on 143
explain: POP3 uses TCP 110 and IMAP uses TCP 143 in their unencrypted forms. Their encrypted versions are POP3S on 995 and IMAPS on 993.

q: Why does NAT hide internal network topology from external hosts?
options: It encrypts all traffic passing through the NAT device
It changes the MAC addresses of internal hosts to a single address
It blocks all inbound traffic by default on every port
External hosts see only the public IP address, not the private addresses of internal hosts
explain: NAT translates private internal addresses to a public address, so outsiders see only the public address and not the internal addressing scheme. This hiding is a side benefit; NAT by itself is not a security control.

q: A new fiber link shows no signal because transmit and receive strands are reversed. How should this be fixed?
options: Replace both switches at either end of the link
Swap the transmit and receive strands at one end so TX connects to RX
Increase the optical transmit power on both interfaces
Reboot both devices to force them to renegotiate polarity
explain: Fiber pairs must cross so that one end's transmit connects to the other end's receive. Swapping the strands at one end, or using correctly keyed polarity, corrects a TX/RX reversal.

q: Why should DHCP scope utilization be monitored?
options: To ensure clients receive the same IP address at every renewal
To track which users are consuming the most bandwidth
To alert administrators before the address pool is exhausted and clients cannot obtain leases
To manually assign reservations for every client on the network
explain: When a DHCP scope runs out of addresses, new clients cannot obtain a lease and appear to have lost connectivity. Monitoring utilization provides warning before exhaustion causes an outage.

q: Why is multi-factor authentication (MFA) important for email accounts?
options: It replaces the need for a strong password on the account
It significantly reduces account takeovers, even when a password is compromised
It encrypts email messages stored in the user's mailbox
It prevents phishing messages from reaching the user's inbox
explain: MFA requires an additional factor beyond the password, so a stolen or phished password alone is usually not enough to take over the account. Phishing-resistant methods such as FIDO2 keys provide the strongest protection.

q: What is statistical multiplexing?
options: Assigning each user a fixed time slot regardless of whether they are transmitting
Reserving a dedicated circuit for each user for the duration of a session
Dividing a channel into fixed frequency bands for each user
Allocating bandwidth dynamically on demand to users who have data to send
explain: Statistical multiplexing shares bandwidth dynamically based on demand, which is efficient for bursty packet traffic. It contrasts with fixed allocation methods such as time-division or frequency-division multiplexing.
